author: nicolas
summary: The 1.2 lexicon update (ADR-0013): rulings G32–G36, 57 primal roots, 22 compounds, 2 function words, 3 frequency correlatives, 24 lexicalised derivations, 2 curated motion metaphors, 3 reglosses, 6 predictable slots activated, and the protected-exceptions label repaired. Applied after 2026-10-17-grammar-rulings by npm run integrate:1.2.

rulings.ruling: When de joins two candidates for owner, the owner is decided in this order: a pronoun, then a personal name (pilo, mare used as names included), then the default of 1.2:G27 (in X de Y, Y is the owner). Pilo de maivo is my father, not father's me. PRONOUN de PRONOUN is allowed, and the right-hand pronoun is the owner: taivo de maivo, you of mine.

yuta + noun phrase names the instrument or means of an action: with, using, by means of. It fills the ADJUNCTS slot like the other prepositions. It never means accompaniment: "with a friend" stays ko.
examples: Maivo lallela li dorbi yuta li kemye.
I open the door with the key.
Li lirayo po yugemeyiya saivo yuta melo.
The singer healed him with music.
Saivori po ka vazranasan yuta benamolu.

rulings.ruling: A quantifier joined to krono with a hyphen gives a frequency adverbial: muya-krono often, poka-krono rarely, rada-krono each time. Like the other -krono correlatives it opens or closes its clause (1.2:G24). The pattern is limited to krono; muya, poka and rada form no other correlatives.
revo-sabesia (know again: recognize) and yave-donuda (give together: share) join revo-vimova and revo-lirala as curated metaphors. The motion prefixes otherwise stay non-productive.

Kinship words are neutral: purma parent, famli sibling, linu child, purmafamli aunt or uncle. Gender is marked only when it matters, by a compound with minva (female) or tarnu (male) where the lexicon has one (minvalinu daughter, tarnufamli brother), and otherwise by the adjective before the noun (minvasan purmafamli, aunt). mare and pilo remain mother and father. Kin by marriage compound with rilde: rildemare mother-in-law. Neither gender root is the negative of the other.
examples: Li tarnufamli de taivo ka corvisan.
